item.title: New trilateral talks on Ukraine war in Abu Dhabi: What to expect?
item.description:
US, Russian, and Ukrainian officials are expected to meet this week in Abu Dhabi for talks on ending the nearly five-year war, but experts cautioned that the meetings were unlikely to yield a major breakthrough. The first direct negotiations in nine months will address “ security guarantees for Ukraine , Europe’s post-war security architecture and economic opportunities to support Ukraine’s reconstruction,” envoy Steve Witkoff said; Washington’s efforts to end the war have been primarily focused on rebuilding commercial ties , though earlier efforts surrounding a potential Alaskan LNG terminal collapsed in response to what US investors described as secret Russian control . “As long as the White House is satisfied with small gestures rather than actual concessions, Putin will not reverse course ,” an Atlantic Council expert wrote. — Brendan Ruberry

Covered by 1 billionaire/family, 2 public.
Sources: Deutsche Welle, France 24, Semafor

item.title: Judge denies motion to dismiss Lindsay Clancy's murder case
item.description:
Massachusetts judge rejects bid by Clancy’s attorneys to have the case against her dismissed A Massachusetts judge cleared the way on Monday for Lindsay Clancy to be tried again on ⁠murder charges for killing her three young children at her home in 2023, saying a retrial would not unconstitutionally subject her to a ⁠double prosecution for the same ⁠crime. Judge William Sullivan in Plymouth rejected a bid by Clancy’s attorneys to have the case against her dismissed. The judge on 4 September declared ⁠a mistrial after the jury reported that a holdout juror was preventing it from reaching a unanimous verdict. Continue reading...

item.title: France accuses Iran of cyber 'sabotage' in fridge attacks
item.description:
France says Iranian military hackers took over refrigeration controllers at around 700 different retail sites last month, turning up temperatures in the middle of the night and spoiling millions of dollars' worth of food. (Image credit: FRED TANNEAU)

item.title: Pope meets with clergy abuse survivors in Argentina
item.description:
Pontiff tells Argentina’s president the economy must benefit all on second stop of 12-day Latin America tour Pope Leo XIV has delivered a stinging critique of Argentine president Javier Milei’s harsh austerity measures, insisting growth must benefit all in a speech met with rapturous applause in Buenos Aires. “The economy must be at the service of the people, rather than people being at the service of the economy,” he said on Sunday, shortly after landing in Argentina on the second leg of a Latin America tour. item.title: Turkey steel factory blast kills at least 17 people
item.description:
At least 16 workers lost their lives in an explosion at a steel factory in Izmir. President Recep Tayyip Erdogan issued an updated casualty toll after a Cabinet meeting.

item.title: Chris Bowen faces a titanic task at Cop31. What will it take for the world to make the climate crisis its top priority? | Adam Morton
item.description:
Whether the global community can bring itself to name fossil fuels as the cause of the climate emergency will be at the centre of debate in Antalya Australian politics could have looked markedly different this week if the Albanese government had succeeded in its longstanding bid to host a major UN climate summit in Adelaide. Tens of thousands of people, including ministers and diplomats representing 200 countries, would have descended on the city of the toxic algal bloom to meet, lobby and negotiate over how to tackle the climate crisis, and wander the halls of a massive green trade fair that runs alongside the formal talks.
